reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2466 a, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ، أَخْبَرَنِي أَبُو الزُّبَيْرِ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ جَابِرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَجَنَازَةُ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ ‏"‏ اهْتَزَّ لَهَا عَرْشُ الرَّحْمَنِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said while the bier of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was before them: "The Throne of the Most Merciful shook for it."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2466 b, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرٌو النَّاقِدُ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ إِدْرِيسَ الأَوْدِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ أَبِي، سُفْيَانُ عَنْ جَابِرٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ اهْتَزَّ عَرْشُ الرَّحْمَنِ لِمَوْتِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Amr al-Naqid narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Idris al-Awdi narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "The Throne of the Most Merciful shook for the death of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2467, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الرُّزِّيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَهَّابِ بْنُ عَطَاءٍ الْخَفَّافُ، عَنْ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ وَجِنَازَتُهُ مَوْضُوعَةٌ - يَعْنِي سَعْدًا - ‏"‏ اهْتَزَّ لَهَا عَرْشُ الرَّحْمَنِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Ruzzi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' al-Khaffaf narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet of Allah (pbuh) said while his bier was placed—meaning Sa'd: "The Throne of the Most Merciful shook for it."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2468 a, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، وَابْنُ، بَشَّارٍ قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ الْبَرَاءَ، يَقُولُ أُهْدِيَتْ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حُلَّةُ حَرِيرٍ فَجَعَلَ أَصْحَابُهُ يَلْمُسُونَهَا وَيَعْجَبُونَ مِنْ لِينِهَا فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَتَعْجَبُونَ مِنْ لِينِ هَذِهِ لَمَنَادِيلُ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ فِي الْجَنَّةِ خَيْرٌ مِنْهَا وَأَلْيَنُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' saying: A silk suit was gifted to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), so his Companions began touching it and marveling at its softness. He said: "Do you marvel at the softness of this? The handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than it and softer."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2468 b, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عَبْدَةَ الضَّبِّيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو دَاوُدَ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، أَنْبَأَنِي أَبُو إِسْحَاقَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ الْبَرَاءَ بْنَ عَازِبٍ، يَقُولُ أُتِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِثَوْبِ حَرِيرٍ ‏.‏ فَذَكَرَ الْحَدِيثَ ثُمَّ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبْدَةَ أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو دَاوُدَ حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ حَدَّثَنِي قَتَادَةُ عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِنَحْوِ هَذَا أَوْ بِمِثْلِهِ ‏.‏
en_text: Ahmad ibn 'Abdah al-Dabbi narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Abu Ishaq informed me, he said: I heard al-Bara' ibn 'Azib saying: A silk garment was brought to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)... and he mentioned the hadith. Then Ibn 'Abdah said: Abu Dawud informed us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to me, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (pbuh), with something like this, or the like of it.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2468 c, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَمْرِو بْنِ جَبَلَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا أُمَيَّةُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، بِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ بِالإِسْنَادَيْنِ جَمِيعًا كَرِوَايَةِ أَبِي دَاوُدَ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Jabalah narrated to us, Umayyah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, this hadith with both chains of narration together, like the narration of Abu Dawud.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2469 a, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا زُهَيْرُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا يُونُسُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شَيْبَانُ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّهُ أُهْدِيَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم جُبَّةٌ مِنْ سُنْدُسٍ وَكَانَ يَنْهَى عَنِ الْحَرِيرِ فَعَجِبَ النَّاسُ مِنْهَا فَقَالَ ‏"‏ وَالَّذِي نَفْسُ مُحَمَّدٍ بِيَدِهِ إِنَّ مَنَادِيلَ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ فِي الْجَنَّةِ أَحْسَنُ مِنْ هَذَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from Qatadah, Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that a robe of fine silk was gifted to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)—and he used to prohibit silk—so the people marveled at it. He said: "By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than this."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2469 b, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سَالِمُ بْنُ نُوحٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ بْنُ عَامِرٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، أَنَّ أُكَيْدِرَ، دُومَةِ الْجَنْدَلِ أَهْدَى لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ حُلَّةً فَذَكَرَ نَحْوَهُ وَلَمْ يَذْكُرْ فِيهِ وَكَانَ يَنْهَى عَنِ الْحَرِيرِ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, Salim ibn Nuh narrated to us, 'Umar ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, that Ukaydir of Dumat al-Jandal gifted a robe to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)... and he mentioned similarly, but he did not mention in it: "and he used to prohibit silk."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2470, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ أَبِي دُجَانَةَ سِمَاكِ بْنِ خَرَشَةَ رضى الله تعالى عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا عَفَّانُ، حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ سَلَمَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا ثَابِتٌ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَخَذَ سَيْفًا يَوْمَ أُحُدٍ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَنْ يَأْخُذُ مِنِّي هَذَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَبَسَطُوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ مِنْهُمْ يَقُولُ أَنَا أَنَا ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَمَنْ يَأْخُذُهُ بِحَقِّهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَحْجَمَ الْقَوْمُ فَقَالَ سِمَاكُ بْنُ خَرَشَةَ أَبُو دُجَانَةَ أَنَا آخُذُهُ بِحَقِّهِ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَخَذَهُ فَفَلَقَ بِهِ هَامَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ ‏.‏
en_text: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) took a sword on the day of Uhud and said: "Who will take this from me?" They stretched out their hands, every person among them saying: "I will, I will." He said: "Who will take it with its due right?" He said: The people hesitated. Then Simak ibn Kharashah, Abu Dujanah, said: "I will take it with its due right." He said: So he took it and cleaved with it the crowns of the idolaters' heads.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2471 a, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ حَرَامٍ وَالِدِ جَابِرٍ رضى الله تعالى عنهما
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ الْقَوَارِيرِيُّ، وَعَمْرٌو النَّاقِدُ، كِلاَهُمَا عَنْ سُفْيَانَ، قَالَ عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ جَابِرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، يَقُولُ لَمَّا كَانَ يَوْمُ أُحُدٍ جِيءَ بِأَبِي مُسَجًّى وَقَدْ مُثِلَ بِهِ - قَالَ - فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَرْفَعَ الثَّوْبَ فَنَهَانِي قَوْمِي ثُمَّ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَرْفَعَ الثَّوْبَ فَنَهَانِي قَوْمِي فَرَفَعَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَوْ أَمَرَ بِهِ فَرُفِعَ فَسَمِعَ صَوْتَ بَاكِيَةٍ أَوْ صَائِحَةٍ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَنْ هَذِهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا بِنْتُ عَمْرٍو أَوْ أُخْتُ عَمْرٍو فَقَالَ ‏"‏ وَلِمَ تَبْكِي فَمَا زَالَتِ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ تُظِلُّهُ بِأَجْنِحَتِهَا حَتَّى رُفِعَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri and 'Amr al-Naqid both narrated to us from Sufyan—'Ubaydullah said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us—he said: I heard Ibn al-Munkadir saying: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: On the day of Uhud, my father was brought covered with a garment, having been mutilated. He said: I wanted to uncover the garment, but my people forbade me; then I wanted to uncover the garment, but my people forbade me. So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) lifted it—or ordered it and it was lifted—and he heard the voice of a weeping woman or screaming woman. He said: "Who is this?" They said: "The daughter of 'Amr—or sister of 'Amr." He said: "Why does she weep? The angels continued to shade him with their wings until he was lifted."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2471 b, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ حَرَامٍ وَالِدِ جَابِرٍ رضى الله تعالى عنهما
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، حَدَّثَنَا وَهْبُ بْنُ جَرِيرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ أُصِيبَ أَبِي يَوْمَ أُحُدٍ فَجَعَلْتُ أَكْشِفُ الثَّوْبَ عَنْ وَجْهِهِ، وَأَبْكِي، وَجَعَلُوا يَنْهَوْنَنِي وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لاَ يَنْهَانِي - قَالَ - وَجَعَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ عَمْرٍو تَبْكِيهِ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ تَبْكِيهِ أَوْ لاَ تَبْكِيهِ مَا زَالَتِ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ تُظِلُّهُ بِأَجْنِحَتِهَا حَتَّى رَفَعْتُمُوهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: My father was struck down on the day of Uhud, so I began uncovering the cloth from his face and weeping, and they began forbidding me while the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) did not forbid me. He said: And Fatimah bint 'Amr began weeping over him, so the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Whether she weeps over him or does not weep over him, the angels continued to shade him with their wings until you lifted him up."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2471 c, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ حَرَامٍ وَالِدِ جَابِرٍ رضى الله تعالى عنهما
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا رَوْحُ بْنُ عُبَادَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ، ح وَحَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ، بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، حَدَّثَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، كِلاَهُمَا عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ، ‏.‏ بِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ غَيْرَ أَنَّ ابْنَ جُرَيْجٍ، لَيْسَ فِي حَدِيثِهِ ذِكْرُ الْمَلاَئِكَةِ وَبُكَاءُ الْبَاكِيَةِ ‏.‏
en_text: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar narrated to us—both of them from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, with this hadith, except that in the hadith of Ibn Jurayj there is no mention of the angels or the weeping of the weeping woman.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2471 d, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ حَرَامٍ وَالِدِ جَابِرٍ رضى الله تعالى عنهما
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي خَلَفٍ، حَدَّثَنَا زَكَرِيَّاءُ بْنُ عَدِيٍّ، أَخْبَرَنَا عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ، بْنُ عَمْرٍو عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ، قَالَ جِيءَ بِأَبِي يَوْمَ أُحُدٍ مُجَدَّعًا فَوُضِعَ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ فَذَكَرَ نَحْوَ حَدِيثِهِمْ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us, Zakariyya' ibn 'Adi narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Amr informed us, from 'Abd al-Karim, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: "My father was brought on the day of Uhud mutilated, and placed before the Prophet (pbuh)..." and he mentioned the like of their hadith.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2472, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ جُلَيْبِيبٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ عُمَرَ بْنِ سَلِيطٍ، حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ كِنَانَةَ، بْنِ نُعَيْمٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَرْزَةَ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ فِي مَغْزًى لَهُ فَأَفَاءَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ لأَصْحَابِهِ ‏"‏ هَلْ تَفْقِدُونَ مِنْ أَحَدٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا نَعَمْ فُلاَنًا وَفُلاَنًا وَفُلاَنًا ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ هَلْ تَفْقِدُونَ مِنْ أَحَدٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا نَعَمْ فُلاَنًا وَفُلاَنًا وَفُلاَنًا ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ هَلْ تَفْقِدُونَ مِنْ أَحَدٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا لاَ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ لَكِنِّي أَفْقِدُ جُلَيْبِيبًا فَاطْلُبُوهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَطُلِبَ فِي الْقَتْلَى فَوَجَدُوهُ إِلَى جَنْبِ سَبْعَةٍ قَدْ قَتَلَهُمْ ثُمَّ قَتَلُوهُ فَأَتَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَوَقَفَ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ قَتَلَ سَبْعَةً ثُمَّ قَتَلُوهُ هَذَا مِنِّي وَأَنَا مِنْهُ هَذَا مِنِّي وَأَنَا مِنْهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَوَضَعَهُ عَلَى سَاعِدَيْهِ لَيْسَ لَهُ إِلاَّ سَاعِدَا النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ فَحُفِرَ لَهُ وَوُضِعَ فِي قَبْرِهِ ‏.‏ وَلَمْ يَذْكُرْ غَسْلاً ‏.‏
en_text: Ishaq ibn 'Umar ibn Salit narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Kinanah ibn Nu'aym, from Abu Barzah, that the Prophet (pbuh) was in an expedition and Allah granted him spoils of war. He said to his Companions, "Are you missing anyone?" They said, "Yes, so-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so." Then he said, "Are you missing anyone?" They said, "Yes, so-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so." Then he said, "Are you missing anyone?" They said, "No." He said, "But I miss Julaybib, so seek him." So he was searched for among the slain, and they found him beside seven whom he had killed, and then they killed him. The Prophet (pbuh) came, stood over him, and said, "He killed seven, then they killed him. This man is of me and I am of him; this man is of me and I am of him." He said: Then he placed him upon his forearms—he had no bed except the forearms of the Prophet (pbuh). He said: So a grave was dug for him and he was placed in his grave. And he did not mention any washing.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2473 a, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا هَدَّابُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ الأَزْدِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ الْمُغِيرَةِ، أَخْبَرَنَا حُمَيْدُ بْنُ هِلاَلٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ، قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ خَرَجْنَا مِنْ قَوْمِنَا غِفَارٍ وَكَانُوا يُحِلُّونَ الشَّهْرَ الْحَرَامَ فَخَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَأَخِي أُنَيْسٌ وَأُمُّنَا فَنَزَلْنَا عَلَى خَالٍ لَنَا فَأَكْرَمَنَا خَالُنَا وَأَحْسَنَ إِلَيْنَا فَحَسَدَنَا قَوْمُهُ فَقَالُوا إِنَّكَ إِذَا خَرَجْتَ عَنْ أَهْلِكَ خَالَفَ إِلَيْهِمْ أُنَيْسٌ فَجَاءَ خَالُنَا فَنَثَا عَلَيْنَا الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَمَّا مَا مَضَى مِنْ مَعْرُوفِكَ فَقَدْ كَدَّرْتَهُ وَلاَ جِمَاعَ لَكَ فِيمَا بَعْدُ ‏.‏ فَقَرَّبْنَا صِرْمَتَنَا فَاحْتَمَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا وَتَغَطَّى خَالُنَا ثَوْبَهُ فَجَعَلَ يَبْكِي فَانْطَلَقْنَا حَتَّى نَزَلْنَا بِحَضْرَةِ مَكَّةَ فَنَافَرَ أُنَيْسٌ عَنْ صِرْمَتِنَا وَعَنْ مِثْلِهَا فَأَتَيَا الْكَاهِنَ فَخَيَّرَ أُنَيْسًا فَأَتَانَا أُنَيْسٌ بِصِرْمَتِنَا وَمِثْلِهَا مَعَهَا - قَالَ - وَقَدْ صَلَّيْتُ يَا ابْنَ أَخِي قَبْلَ أَنْ أَلْقَى رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِثَلاَثِ سِنِينَ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ لِمَنْ قَالَ لِلَّهِ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ فَأَيْنَ تَوَجَّهُ قَالَ أَتَوَجَّهُ حَيْثُ يُوَجِّهُنِي رَبِّي أُصَلِّي عِشَاءً حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ مِنْ آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ أُلْقِيتُ كَأَنِّي خِفَاءٌ حَتَّى تَعْلُوَنِي الشَّمْسُ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ أُنَيْسٌ إِنَّ لِي حَاجَةً بِمَكَّةَ فَاكْفِنِي ‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقَ أُنَيْسٌ حَتَّى أَتَى مَكَّةَ فَرَاثَ عَلَىَّ ثُمَّ جَاءَ فَقُلْتُ مَا صَنَعْتَ قَالَ لَقِيتُ رَجُلاً بِمَكَّةَ عَلَى دِينِكَ يَزْعُمُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَرْسَلَهُ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ فَمَا يَقُولُ النَّاسُ قَالَ يَقُولُونَ شَاعِرٌ كَاهِنٌ سَاحِرٌ ‏.‏ وَكَانَ أُنَيْسٌ أَحَدَ الشُّعَرَاءِ ‏.‏ قَالَ أُنَيْسٌ لَقَدْ سَمِعْتُ قَوْلَ الْكَهَنَةِ فَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِهِمْ وَلَقَدْ وَضَعْتُ قَوْلَهُ عَلَى أَقْرَاءِ الشِّعْرِ فَمَا يَلْتَئِمُ عَلَى لِسَانِ أَحَدٍ بَعْدِي أَنَّهُ شِعْرٌ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَصَادِقٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ فَاكْفِنِي حَتَّى أَذْهَبَ فَأَنْظُرَ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَتَيْتُ مَكَّةَ فَتَضَعَّفْتُ رَجُلاً مِنْهُمْ فَقُلْتُ أَيْنَ هَذَا الَّذِي تَدْعُونَهُ الصَّابِئَ فَأَشَارَ إِلَىَّ فَقَالَ الصَّابِئَ ‏.‏ فَمَالَ عَلَىَّ أَهْلُ الْوَادِي بِكُلِّ مَدَرَةٍ وَعَظْمٍ حَتَّى خَرَرْتُ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَىَّ - قَالَ - فَارْتَفَعْتُ حِينَ ارْتَفَعْتُ كَأَنِّي نُصُبٌ أَحْمَرُ - قَالَ - فَأَتَيْتُ زَمْزَمَ فَغَسَلْتُ عَنِّي الدِّمَاءَ وَشَرِبْتُ مِنْ مَائِهَا وَلَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ يَا ابْنَ أَخِي ثَلاَثِينَ بَيْنَ لَيْلَةٍ وَيَوْمٍ مَا كَانَ لِي طَعَامٌ إِلاَّ مَاءُ زَمْزَمَ فَسَمِنْتُ حَتَّى تَكَسَّرَتْ عُكَنُ بَطْنِي وَمَا وَجَدْتُ عَلَى كَبِدِي سُخْفَةَ جُوعٍ - قَالَ - فَبَيْنَا أَهْلُ مَكَّةَ فِي لَيْلَةٍ قَمْرَاءَ إِضْحِيَانَ إِذْ ضُرِبَ عَلَى أَسْمِخَتِهِمْ فَمَا يَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ أَحَدٌ وَامْرَأَتَيْنِ مِنْهُمْ تَدْعُوَانِ إِسَافًا وَنَائِلَةَ - قَالَ - فَأَتَتَا عَلَىَّ فِي طَوَافِهِمَا فَقُلْتُ أَنْكِحَا أَحَدَهُمَا الأُخْرَى - قَالَ - فَمَا تَنَاهَتَا عَنْ قَوْلِهِمَا - قَالَ - فَأَتَتَا عَلَىَّ فَقُلْتُ هَنٌ مِثْلُ الْخَشَبَةِ غَيْرَ أَنِّي لاَ أَكْنِي ‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقَتَا تُوَلْوِلاَنِ وَتَقُولاَنِ لَوْ كَانَ هَا هُنَا أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَنْفَارِنَا ‏.‏ قَالَ فَاسْتَقْبَلَهُمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ وَهُمَا هَابِطَانِ قَالَ ‏"‏ مَا لَكُمَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَتَا الصَّابِئُ بَيْنَ الْكَعْبَةِ وَأَسْتَارِهَا قَالَ ‏"‏ مَا قَالَ لَكُمَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَتَا إِنَّهُ قَالَ لَنَا كَلِمَةً تَمْلأُ الْفَمَ ‏.‏ وَجَاءَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى اسْتَلَمَ الْحَجَرَ وَطَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ هُوَ وَصَاحِبُهُ ثُمَّ صَلَّى فَلَمَّا قَضَى صَلاَتَهُ قَالَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ ‏.‏ فَكُنْتُ أَنَا أَوَّلُ مَنْ حَيَّاهُ بِتَحِيَّةِ الإِسْلاَمِ - قَالَ - فَقُلْتُ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ وَعَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ مَنْ أَنْتَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ مِنْ غِفَارٍ - قَالَ - فَأَهْوَى بِيَدِهِ فَوَضَعَ أَصَابِعَهُ عَلَى جَبْهَتِهِ فَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي كَرِهَ أَنِ انْتَمَيْتُ إِلَى غِفَارٍ ‏.‏ فَذَهَبْتُ آخُذُ بِيَدِهِ فَقَدَعَنِي صَاحِبُهُ وَكَانَ أَعْلَمَ بِهِ مِنِّي ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ مَتَى كُنْتَ هَا هُنَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ قَدْ كُنْتُ هَا هُنَا مُنْذُ ثَلاَثِينَ بَيْنَ لَيْلَةٍ وَيَوْمٍ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَمَنْ كَانَ يُطْعِمُكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ مَا كَانَ لِي طَعَامٌ إِلاَّ مَاءُ زَمْزَمَ ‏.‏ فَسَمِنْتُ حَتَّى تَكَسَّرَتْ عُكَنُ بَطْنِي وَمَا أَجِدُ عَلَى كَبِدِي سُخْفَةَ جُوعٍ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّهَا مُبَارَكَةٌ إِنَّهَا طَعَامُ طُعْمٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ائْذَنْ لِي فِي طَعَامِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ ‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ وَانْطَلَقْتُ مَعَهُمَا فَفَتَحَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ بَابًا فَجَعَلَ يَقْبِضُ لَنَا مِنْ زَبِيبِ الطَّائِفِ وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ أَوَّلَ طَعَامٍ أَكَلْتُهُ بِهَا ثُمَّ غَبَرْتُ مَا غَبَرْتُ ثُمَّ أَتَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّهُ قَدْ وُجِّهَتْ لِي أَرْضٌ ذَاتُ نَخْلٍ لاَ أُرَاهَا إِلاَّ يَثْرِبَ فَهَلْ أَنْتَ مُبَلِّغٌ عَنِّي قَوْمَكَ عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَنْفَعَهُمْ بِكَ وَيَأْجُرَكَ فِيهِمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَأَتَيْتُ أُنَيْسًا فَقَالَ مَا صَنَعْتَ قُلْتُ صَنَعْتُ أَنِّي قَدْ أَسْلَمْتُ وَصَدَّقْتُ ‏.‏ قَالَ مَا بِي رَغْبَةٌ عَنْ دِينِكَ فَإِنِّي قَدْ أَسْلَمْتُ وَصَدَّقْتُ ‏.‏ فَأَتَيْنَا أُمَّنَا فَقَالَتْ مَا بِي رَغْبَةٌ عَنْ دِينِكُمَا فَإِنِّي قَدْ أَسْلَمْتُ وَصَدَّقْتُ ‏.‏ فَاحْتَمَلْنَا حَتَّى أَتَيْنَا قَوْمَنَا غِفَارًا فَأَسْلَمَ نِصْفُهُمْ وَكَانَ يَؤُمُّهُمْ إِيمَاءُ بْنُ رَحَضَةَ الْغِفَارِيُّ وَكَانَ سَيِّدَهُمْ ‏.‏ وَقَالَ نِصْفُهُمْ إِذَا قَدِمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمَدِينَةَ أَسْلَمْنَا ‏.‏ فَقَدِمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمَدِينَةَ فَأَسْلَمَ نِصْفُهُمُ الْبَاقِي وَجَاءَتْ أَسْلَمُ فَقَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِخْوَتُنَا نُسْلِمُ عَلَى الَّذِي أَسْلَمُوا عَلَيْهِ ‏.‏ فَأَسْلَمُوا فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ غِفَارُ غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَهَا وَأَسْلَمُ سَالَمَهَا اللَّهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Haddab ibn Khalid al-Azdi narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Humayd ibn Hilal informed us, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, who said: Abu Dharr said: We departed from our people Ghifar—and they used to make the sacred month lawful. So I departed, along with my brother Unays and our mother, and we stayed with a maternal uncle of ours. Our maternal uncle honored us and treated us well. But his people envied us and said: "Whenever you leave your family, Unays goes behind your back to them." So our maternal uncle came and relayed to us what had been said to him. I said to him: "As for your past kindness, you have ruined it, and there can be no union between us hereafter." So we brought our herd of livestock close, loaded onto them, and our maternal uncle covered himself with his garment and began to weep. We departed until we settled in the vicinity of Mecca. Unays then competed in a contest of poetic boasting for our herd and an equal amount to match it. They both went to the soothsayer, who judged in favor of Unays. So Unays came to us with our herd and an equal herd along with it. He said: And I had already been praying, O son of my brother, three years before meeting the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). I said, "To whom?" He said, "To Allah." I said, "So where did you face?" He said, "I faced wherever my Lord directed me. I would pray late into the evening until, toward the end of the night, I would collapse as if I were a piece of cloth until the sun rose over me." Then Unays said: "I have some business in Mecca, so look after my affairs." Unays departed until he reached Mecca, but he was delayed in returning to me. Then he arrived, and I said: "What did you do?" He said: "I met a man in Mecca upon your religion, who claims that Allah has sent him." I said: "So what do the people say?" He said: "They say: a poet, a soothsayer, a sorcerer." And Unays was one of the poets. Unays said: "I have heard the speech of the soothsayers, and it is not their speech. And I measured his speech against the meters of poetry, and it does not conform to the tongue of anyone after me to say that it is poetry. By Allah, he is truly truthful, and they are liars!" He said: I said, "So look after my affairs until I go and see." He said: So I came to Mecca, and I approached a man among them whom I deemed weak and said: "Where is this one whom you call the Sabaean?" He pointed at me and shouted: "The Sabaean!" Thereupon the people of the valley turned against me with every clod of earth and bone until I fell down unconscious. He said: When I arose, I arose looking like a red sacrificial stone. He said: So I came to Zamzam, washed the blood off myself, and drank of its water. And indeed, O son of my brother, I stayed for thirty, between night and day, having no food except Zamzam water. I grew so fat that the folds of my belly creased, and I felt no weakness of hunger in my liver. He said: While the people of Mecca were in a bright, moonlit night, when a slumber fell upon their ears, so that no one was circumambulating the House except two women from among them who were calling upon Isaf and Na'ilah. He said: They passed by me in their circumambulation, and I said: "Marry one to the other!" He said: But they did not desist from their words. He said: They passed by me again, and I said: "[An idol with] a private organ like a piece of wood—except that I did not speak euphemistically." So they turned away wailing and saying: "If only there were someone here from our men!" He said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and Abu Bakr met them as the two were descending. He said: "What is the matter with you two?" They said: "The Sabaean between the Ka'bah and its coverings!" He said: "What did he say to you two?" They said: "He spoke to us a foul word that fills the mouth." And the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) came until he touched the Black Stone and circumambulated the House, he and his companion, then he prayed. When he finished his prayer—Abu Dharr said—I was the first person to greet him with the greeting of Islam. He said: I said, "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "And upon you, and the mercy of Allah." Then he said: "Who are you?" He said: I said, "From Ghifar." He said: He moved his hand and placed his fingers upon his forehead. I said to myself: "He disliked that I affiliated myself with Ghifar." So I went to take his hand, but his companion restrained me—and he knew him better than I did. Then he raised his head and said: "When did you arrive here?" He said: I said, "I have been here for thirty, between night and day." He said: "And who has been feeding you?" He said: I said, "I had no food except Zamzam water, and I have grown fat until the folds of my belly creased, and I do not feel any weakness of hunger in my liver." He said: "Indeed, it is blessed; it is food that nourishes." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to host him tonight." So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and Abu Bakr set out, and I set out with them. Abu Bakr opened a door and began taking handfuls of raisins of al-Ta'if for us, and that was the first food I ate there. Then I remained for as long as I remained, then I came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and he said: "A land of date palms has been shown to me; I see it to be none other than Yathrib. Will you convey from me to your people? Perhaps Allah will benefit them through you and reward you regarding them." So I came to Unays, and he said: "What did you do?" I said: "I have embraced Islam and believed." He said: "I have no dislike for your religion; indeed, I too have embraced Islam and believed." Then we came to our mother, and she said: "I have no dislike for the religion of you two; indeed, I too have embraced Islam and believed." So we loaded up until we reached our people Ghifar, and half of them embraced Islam. They were led in prayer by Imah ibn Rahadah al-Ghifari, and he was their leader. And half of them said: "When the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) arrives in Medina, we will embrace Islam." So when the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) arrived in Medina, the remaining half embraced Islam. And the tribe of Aslam came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, our brothers; we embrace Islam upon that which they embraced Islam." So they embraced Islam. Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Ghifar—may Allah forgive them; and Aslam—may Allah preserve them in peace."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2473 b, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْحَنْظَلِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا النَّضْرُ بْنُ شُمَيْلٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ، بْنُ الْمُغِيرَةِ حَدَّثَنَا حُمَيْدُ بْنُ هِلاَلٍ، بِهَذَا الإِسْنَادِ وَزَادَ بَعْدَ قَوْلِهِ قُلْتُ فَاكْفِنِي حَتَّى أَذْهَبَ فَأَنْظُرَ ‏.‏ قَالَ نَعَمْ وَكُنْ عَلَى حَذَرٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ فَإِنَّهُمْ قَدْ شَنِفُوا لَهُ وَتَجَهَّمُوا ‏.‏
en_text: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Humayd ibn Hilal narrated to us, with this chain of narration; and he added after his statement: "I said: So look after my affairs until I go and see." He said: "Yes, and be cautious of the people of Mecca, for they have become hateful and hostile toward him."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2473 c, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى الْعَنَزِيُّ، حَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي عَدِيٍّ، قَالَ أَنْبَأَنَا ابْنُ عَوْنٍ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ، قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ يَا ابْنَ أَخِي صَلَّيْتُ سَنَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ مَبْعَثِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ فَأَيْنَ كُنْتَ تَوَجَّهُ قَالَ حَيْثُ وَجَّهَنِيَ اللَّهُ ‏.‏ وَاقْتَصَّ الْحَدِيثَ بِنَحْوِ حَدِيثِ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ وَقَالَ فِي الْحَدِيثِ فَتَنَافَرَا إِلَى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْكُهَّانِ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ أَخِي أُنَيْسٌ يَمْدَحُهُ حَتَّى غَلَبَهُ - قَالَ - فَأَخَذْنَا صِرْمَتَهُ فَضَمَمْنَاهَا إِلَى صِرْمَتِنَا ‏.‏ وَقَالَ أَيْضًا فِي حَدِيثِهِ قَالَ فَجَاءَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَطَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ وَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ خَلْفَ الْمَقَامِ - قَالَ - فَأَتَيْتُهُ فَإِنِّي لأَوَّلُ النَّاسِ حَيَّاهُ بِتَحِيَّةِ الإِسْلاَمِ - قَالَ - قُلْتُ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَعَلَيْكَ السَّلاَمُ مَنْ أَنْتَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَفِي حَدِيثِهِ أَيْضًا فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مُنْذُ كَمْ أَنْتَ هَا هُنَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ مُنْذُ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ ‏.‏ وَفِيهِ فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ أَتْحِفْنِي بِضِيَافَتِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anazi narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to me, he said: Ibn 'Awn informed us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, who said: Abu Dharr said: "O son of my brother, I used to pray two years before the mission of the Prophet (pbuh)." He said: I asked, "So where did you face?" He said: "Wherever Allah directed me." And he related the hadith similar to the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, and in the hadith he said: "So the two of them went for arbitration to a man from among the soothsayers." He said: "My brother Unays kept praising him until he overcame him." He said: "So we took his herd of livestock and added it to our herd." And he also said in his hadith: He said: Then the Prophet (pbuh) came and circumambulated the House and prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam. He said: So I came to him, and I was the first person to greet him with the greeting of Islam. He said: I said, "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "And upon you be peace; who are you?" And in his hadith also: He said, "How long have you been here?" He said: I said, "For fifteen." And in it: Abu Bakr said, "Grant me the honor of hosting him tonight."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2474, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنِي إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنُ عَرْعَرَةَ السَّامِيُّ، وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ، - وَتَقَارَبَا فِي سِيَاقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَاللَّفْظُ لاِبْنِ حَاتِمٍ - قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ مَهْدِيٍّ حَدَّثَنَا الْمُثَنَّى بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَمْرَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ لَمَّا بَلَغَ أَبَا ذَرٍّ مَبْعَثُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِمَكَّةَ قَالَ لأَخِيهِ ارْكَبْ إِلَى هَذَا الْوَادِي فَاعْلَمْ لِي عِلْمَ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ يَأْتِيهِ الْخَبَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَاسْمَعْ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ ثُمَّ ائْتِنِي ‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقَ الآخَرُ حَتَّى قَدِمَ مَكَّةَ وَسَمِعَ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى أَبِي ذَرٍّ فَقَالَ رَأَيْتُهُ يَأْمُرُ بِمَكَارِمِ الأَخْلاَقِ وَكَلاَمًا مَا هُوَ بِالشِّعْرِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ مَا شَفَيْتَنِي فِيمَا أَرَدْتُ ‏.‏ فَتَزَوَّدَ وَحَمَلَ شَنَّةً لَهُ فِيهَا مَاءٌ حَتَّى قَدِمَ مَكَّةَ فَأَتَى الْمَسْجِدَ فَالْتَمَسَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَلاَ يَعْرِفُهُ وَكَرِهَ أَنْ يَسْأَلَ عَنْهُ حَتَّى أَدْرَكَهُ - يَعْنِي اللَّيْلَ - فَاضْطَجَعَ فَرَآهُ عَلِيٌّ فَعَرَفَ أَنَّهُ غَرِيبٌ فَلَمَّا رَآهُ تَبِعَهُ فَلَمْ يَسْأَلْ وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمَا صَاحِبَهُ عَنْ شَىْءٍ حَتَّى أَصْبَحَ ثُمَّ احْتَمَلَ قُرَيْبَتَهُ وَزَادَهُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ فَظَلَّ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ وَلاَ يَرَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى أَمْسَى فَعَادَ إِلَى مَضْجَعِهِ فَمَرَّ بِهِ عَلِيٌّ فَقَالَ مَا أَنَى لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَعْلَمَ مَنْزِلَهُ فَأَقَامَهُ فَذَهَبَ بِهِ مَعَهُ وَلاَ يَسْأَلُ وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمَا صَاحِبَهُ عَنْ شَىْءٍ حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الثَّالِثِ فَعَلَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ فَأَقَامَهُ عَلِيٌّ مَعَهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ أَلاَ تُحَدِّثُنِي مَا الَّذِي أَقْدَمَكَ هَذَا الْبَلَدَ قَالَ إِنْ أَعْطَيْتَنِي عَهْدًا وَمِيثَاقًا لَتُرْشِدَنِّي فَعَلْتُ ‏.‏ فَفَعَلَ فَأَخْبَرَهُ فَقَالَ فَإِنَّهُ حَقٌّ وَهُوَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَإِذَا أَصْبَحْتَ فَاتَّبِعْنِي فَإِنِّي إِنْ رَأَيْتُ شَيْئًا أَخَافُ عَلَيْكَ قُمْتُ كَأَنِّي أُرِيقُ الْمَاءَ فَإِنْ مَضَيْتُ فَاتَّبِعْنِي حَتَّى تَدْخُلَ مَدْخَلِي ‏.‏ فَفَعَلَ فَانْطَلَقَ يَقْفُوهُ حَتَّى دَخَلَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ فَسَمِعَ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ وَأَسْلَمَ مَكَانَهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ ارْجِعْ إِلَى قَوْمِكَ فَأَخْبِرْهُمْ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَكَ أَمْرِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لأَصْرُخَنَّ بِهَا بَيْنَ ظَهْرَانَيْهِمْ ‏.‏ فَخَرَجَ حَتَّى أَتَى الْمَسْجِدَ فَنَادَى بِأَعْلَى صَوْتِهِ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ‏.‏ وَثَارَ الْقَوْمُ فَضَرَبُوهُ حَتَّى أَضْجَعُوهُ فَأَتَى الْعَبَّاسُ فَأَكَبَّ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ وَيْلَكُمْ أَلَسْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ مِنْ غِفَارٍ وَأَنَّ طَرِيقَ تُجَّارِكُمْ إِلَى الشَّامِ عَلَيْهِمْ ‏.‏ فَأَنْقَذَهُ مِنْهُمْ ثُمَّ عَادَ مِنَ الْغَدِ بِمِثْلِهَا وَثَارُوا إِلَيْهِ فَضَرَبُوهُ فَأَكَبَّ عَلَيْهِ الْعَبَّاسُ فَأَنْقَذَهُ ‏.‏
en_text: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah al-Sami and Muhammad ibn Hatim both narrated to me—and their narrations were close in context, with the wording being Ibn Hatim's—they said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, al-Muthanna ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Jamrah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When news of the Prophet's (pbuh) mission reached Abu Dharr in Mecca, he said to his brother: "Ride to this valley and find out for me about this man who claims that news comes to him from heaven, listen to his words, and then come back to me." So the other set out until he reached Mecca, listened to his words, and then returned to Abu Dharr and said: "I saw him enjoining noble character traits, and speech that is not poetry." Abu Dharr said: "You have not satisfied me regarding what I wanted." So he packed provisions and took a small waterskin of his containing water until he reached Mecca. He came to the mosque and sought the Prophet (pbuh), while he did not know him and disliked asking about him, until it overtook him—meaning night. So he lay down, and 'Ali saw him and recognized that he was a stranger. When he saw him, he followed him, but neither of them asked the other about anything until morning came. Then he carried his small waterskin and his provisions to the mosque, and spent that day without seeing the Prophet (pbuh) until evening came. Then he returned to his sleeping place, and 'Ali passed by him and said: "Has the time not come for the man to know his dwelling place?" So he made him stand up and took him with him, and neither of them asked the other about anything until the third day arrived, when he did the same. 'Ali made him stand up with him, then said to him: "Will you not tell me what brought you to this land?" He said: "If you give me a covenant and a pledge that you will guide me, I will do so." 'Ali did so, and he informed him. 'Ali said: "Indeed, it is true, and he is the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). So when morning comes, follow me; if I see anything that I fear for you, I will stand as if I am passing water. If I proceed, then follow me until you enter where I enter." He did so, and set out following his tracks until he entered upon the Prophet (pbuh), and Abu Dharr entered with him. He listened to his words and embraced Islam on the spot. The Prophet (pbuh) said to him: "Return to your people and inform them until my command reaches you." He said: "By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I shall shout it aloud among them!" So he went out until he reached the mosque, and cried out at the top of his voice: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah!" The people rose against him and beat him until they knocked him down. Then al-'Abbas came, threw himself over him, and said: "Woe to you! Do you not know that he is from Ghifar, and that your merchants' route to Sham passes by them?" So he rescued him from them. Then he returned the next day and did the same, and they rose against him and beat him, and al-'Abbas threw himself over him and rescued him.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2475 a, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رضى الله تعالى عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ يَحْيَى، أَخْبَرَنَا خَالِدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ بَيَانٍ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ أَبِي، حَازِمٍ عَنْ جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، ح وَحَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الْحَمِيدِ بْنُ بَيَانٍ، حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدٌ، عَنْ بَيَانٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ قَيْسَ بْنَ أَبِي، حَازِمٍ يَقُولُ قَالَ جَرِيرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ مَا حَجَبَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُنْذُ أَسْلَمْتُ وَلاَ رَآنِي إِلاَّ ضَحِكَ ‏.‏
en_text: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Khalid ibn 'Abdullah informed us, from Bayan, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir ibn 'Abdullah; (H) and 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to me, Khalid narrated to us, from Bayan, who said: I heard Qays ibn Abi Hazim saying: Jarir ibn 'Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) never screened himself from me since I embraced Islam, nor did he see me without smiling.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2475 b, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رضى الله تعالى عنه ‏‏
text_original: وَحَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا وَكِيعٌ، وَأَبُو أُسَامَةَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، ح وَحَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ نُمَيْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ إِدْرِيسَ، حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، عَنْ قَيْسٍ، عَنْ جَرِيرٍ، قَالَ مَا حَجَبَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُنْذُ أَسْلَمْتُ وَلاَ رَآنِي إِلاَّ تَبَسَّمَ فِي وَجْهِي ‏.‏ زَادَ ابْنُ نُمَيْرٍ فِي حَدِيثِهِ عَنِ ابْنِ إِدْرِيسَ وَلَقَدْ شَكَوْتُ إِلَيْهِ أَنِّي لاَ أَثْبُتُ عَلَى الْخَيْلِ فَضَرَبَ بِيَدِهِ فِي صَدْرِي وَقَالَ ‏"‏ اللَّهُمَّ ثَبِّتْهُ وَاجْعَلْهُ هَادِيًا مَهْدِيًّا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' and Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Isma'il; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us, from Qays, from Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) never screened himself from me since I embraced Islam, nor did he look at me without smiling in my face. Ibn Numayr added in his narration from Ibn Idris: "And I complained to him that I could not sit firmly on horses, so he struck his hand upon my chest and said: 'O Allah, keep him firm and make him a guide who is guided.'"

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2476 a, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رضى الله تعالى عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الْحَمِيدِ بْنُ بَيَانٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا خَالِدٌ، عَنْ بَيَانٍ، عَنْ قَيْسٍ، عَنْ جَرِيرٍ، قَالَ كَانَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ بَيْتٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ ذُو الْخَلَصَةِ وَكَانَ يُقَالُ لَهُ الْكَعْبَةُ الْيَمَانِيَةُ وَالْكَعْبَةُ الشَّامِيَّةُ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ هَلْ أَنْتَ مُرِيحِي مِنْ ذِي الْخَلَصَةِ وَالْكَعْبَةِ الْيَمَانِيَةِ وَالشَّامِيَّةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَنَفَرْتُ إِلَيْهِ فِي مِائَةٍ وَخَمْسِينَ مِنْ أَحْمَسَ فَكَسَرْنَاهُ وَقَتَلْنَا مَنْ وَجَدْنَا عِنْدَهُ فَأَتَيْتُهُ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ - قَالَ - فَدَعَا لَنَا وَلأَحْمَسَ ‏.‏
en_text: Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to me, Khalid informed us, from Bayan, from Qays, from Jarir, who said: In the pre-Islamic days of ignorance there was a house called Dhu al-Khalasah, and it was also called the Yemeni Ka'bah and the Sham Ka'bah. The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Will you not relieve me of Dhu al-Khalasah and the Yemeni and Sham Ka'bah?" So I set out to it with one hundred and fifty from Ahmas, and we demolished it and killed whomever we found at it. Then I came to him and informed him. He said: So he supplicated for us and for Ahmas.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2476 b, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رضى الله تعالى عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَخْبَرَنَا جَرِيرٌ، عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَبِي خَالِدٍ، عَنْ قَيْسِ، بْنِ أَبِي حَازِمٍ عَنْ جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْبَجَلِيِّ، قَالَ قَالَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ يَا جَرِيرُ أَلاَ تُرِيحُنِي مِنْ ذِي الْخَلَصَةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ بَيْتٍ لِخَثْعَمَ كَانَ يُدْعَى كَعْبَةَ الْيَمَانِيَةِ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَنَفَرْتُ فِي خَمْسِينَ وَمِائَةِ فَارِسٍ وَكُنْتُ لاَ أَثْبُتُ عَلَى الْخَيْلِ فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَضَرَبَ يَدَهُ فِي صَدْرِي فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اللَّهُمَّ ثَبِّتْهُ وَاجْعَلْهُ هَادِيًا مَهْدِيًّا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَانْطَلَقَ فَحَرَّقَهَا بِالنَّارِ ثُمَّ بَعَثَ جَرِيرٌ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَجُلاً يُبَشِّرُهُ يُكْنَى أَبَا أَرْطَاةَ مِنَّا فَأَتَى رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ لَهُ مَا جِئْتُكَ حَتَّى تَرَكْنَاهَا كَأَنَّهَا جَمَلٌ أَجْرَبُ ‏.‏ فَبَرَّكَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى خَيْلِ أَحْمَسَ وَرِجَالِهَا خَمْسَ مَرَّاتٍ ‏.‏
en_text: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir informed us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir ibn 'Abdullah al-Bajali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to me: "O Jarir, will you not relieve me of Dhu al-Khalasah?"—a house belonging to Khath'am that was called the Ka'bah of Yemen. He said: So I set out with one hundred and fifty horsemen. I could not sit firmly on horses, so I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), and he struck his hand upon my chest and said: "O Allah, keep him firm and make him a guide who is guided." He said: So he went and burned it down with fire. Then Jarir sent a man from among us with the kunyah Abu Artah to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) to convey the glad tidings. He came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and said to him: "I have not come to you until we left it looking like a mangy camel." Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) invoked blessings upon the horses of Ahmas and its men five times.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2476 c, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رضى الله تعالى عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا وَكِيعٌ، ح وَحَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ نُمَيْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي ح، وَحَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبَّادٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، ح وَحَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ أَبِي عُمَرَ، حَدَّثَنَا مَرْوَانُ، - يَعْنِي الْفَزَارِيَّ ح وَحَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ رَافِعٍ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ، كُلُّهُمْ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، بِهَذَا الإِسْنَادِ وَقَالَ فِي حَدِيثِ مَرْوَانَ فَجَاءَ بَشِيرُ جَرِيرٍ أَبُو أَرْطَاةَ حُصَيْنُ بْنُ رَبِيعَةَ يُبَشِّرُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
en_text: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Marwan—meaning al-Fazari—narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, Abu Usamah narrated to us—all of them from Isma'il, with this chain of narration. And in the hadith of Marwan he said: "Then Jarir's bearer of glad tidings, Abu Artah Husayn ibn Rabi'ah, came conveying glad tidings to the Prophet (pbuh)."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2477, book 44, باب فَضَائِلِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رضى الله عنهما ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا زُهَيْرُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، وَأَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ النَّضْرِ قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا هَاشِمُ بْنُ الْقَاسِمِ، حَدَّثَنَا وَرْقَاءُ بْنُ عُمَرَ الْيَشْكُرِيُّ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عُبَيْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ أَبِي يَزِيدَ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، أَنَّوسلم أَتَى الْخَلاَءَ فَوَضَعْتُ لَهُ وَضُوءًا فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ قَالَ ‏"‏ مَنْ وَضَعَ هَذَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فِي رِوَايَةِ زُهَيْرٍ قَالُوا ‏.‏ وَفِي رِوَايَةِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ قُلْتُ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ اللَّهُمَّ فَقِّهْهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Zuhayr ibn Harb and Abu Bakr ibn al-Nadr both narrated to us—they said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Warqa' ibn 'Umar al-Yashkuri narrated to us, he said: I heard 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid narrating from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (pbuh) entered the privy, so I placed ablution water for him. When he came out, he said, "Who placed this?" In the narration of Zuhayr: they said; and in the narration of Abu Bakr: I said, "Ibn 'Abbas." He said: "O Allah, grant him deep understanding of the religion."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2478, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رضى الله عنهما ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الرَّبِيعِ الْعَتَكِيُّ، وَخَلَفُ بْنُ هِشَامٍ، وَأَبُو كَامِلٍ الْجَحْدَرِيُّ كُلُّهُمْ عَنْ حَمَّادِ، بْنِ زَيْدٍ - قَالَ أَبُو الرَّبِيعِ حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، - حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ رَأَيْتُ فِي الْمَنَامِ كَأَنَّ فِي يَدِي قِطْعَةَ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ وَلَيْسَ مَكَانٌ أُرِيدُ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ إِلاَّ طَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ - قَالَ - فَقَصَصْتُهُ عَلَى حَفْصَةَ فَقَصَّتْهُ حَفْصَةُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَرَى عَبْدَ اللَّهِ رَجُلاً صَالِحًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki, Khalaf ibn Hisham, and Abu Kamil al-Jahdari all narrated to us from Hammad ibn Zayd—Abu al-Rabi' said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us—Ayyub narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I saw in a dream as if there were in my hand a piece of fine silk brocade, and there was no place in Paradise that I wished for except that it flew to it. He said: So I related it to Hafsah, and Hafsah related it to the Prophet (pbuh), and the Prophet (pbuh) said: "I see 'Abdullah as a righteous man."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2479 a, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رضى الله عنهما ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَبْدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، - وَاللَّفْظُ لِعَبْدٍ - قَالاَ أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ، الرَّزَّاقِ أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ سَالِمٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ كَانَ الرَّجُلُ فِي حَيَاةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا رَأَى رُؤْيَا قَصَّهَا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَتَمَنَّيْتُ أَنْ أَرَى رُؤْيَا أَقُصُّهَا عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ وَكُنْتُ غُلاَمًا شَابًّا عَزَبًا وَكُنْتُ أَنَامُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَرَأَيْتُ فِي النَّوْمِ كَأَنَّ مَلَكَيْنِ أَخَذَانِي فَذَهَبَا بِي إِلَى النَّارِ فَإِذَا هِيَ مَطْوِيَّةٌ كَطَىِّ الْبِئْرِ وَإِذَا لَهَا قَرْنَانِ كَقَرْنَىِ الْبِئْرِ وَإِذَا فِيهَا نَاسٌ قَدْ عَرَفْتُهُمْ فَجَعَلْتُ أَقُولُ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ - قَالَ - فَلَقِيَهُمَا مَلَكٌ فَقَالَ لِي لَمْ تُرَعْ ‏.‏ فَقَصَصْتُهَا عَلَى حَفْصَةَ فَقَصَّتْهَا حَفْصَةُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ لَوْ كَانَ يُصَلِّي مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ سَالِمٌ فَكَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ لاَ يَنَامُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً ‏.‏
en_text: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—and the wording is 'Abd's—they said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: During the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), whenever a person saw a dream, he would relate it to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). So I wished that I would see a dream that I could relate to the Prophet (pbuh). He said: And I was a young, unmarried youth, and I used to sleep in the mosque during the time of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). Then I saw in sleep as if two angels took me and went with me to the Fire, and behold, it was cased like the casing of a well, and behold, it had two horns like the two horns of a well, and behold, inside it were people I recognized. So I began saying, "I seek refuge with Allah from the Fire! I seek refuge with Allah from the Fire! I seek refuge with Allah from the Fire!" He said: Then an angel met them both and said to me, "Do not fear." So I related it to Hafsah, and Hafsah related it to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). The Prophet (pbuh) said: "What an excellent man 'Abdullah is, if only he would pray during the night." Salim said: After that, 'Abdullah would not sleep at night except a little.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2479 b, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رضى الله عنهما ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ الدَّارِمِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ خَالِدٍ، خَتَنُ الْفِرْيَابِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ الْفَزَارِيِّ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ كُنْتُ أَبِيتُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لِي أَهْلٌ فَرَأَيْتُ فِي الْمَنَامِ كَأَنَّمَا انْطُلِقَ بِي إِلَى بِئْرٍ ‏.‏ فَذَكَرَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِمَعْنَى حَدِيثِ الزُّهْرِيِّ عَنْ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ ‏.‏
en_text: Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us, Musa ibn Khalid, son-in-law of al-Firyabi, informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I used to stay overnight in the mosque and had no family. Then I saw in a dream as if I were taken to a well... and he mentioned from the Prophet (pbuh) with the meaning of the hadith of al-Zuhri from Salim from his father.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2480 a, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، وَابْنُ، بَشَّارٍ قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، سَمِعْتُ قَتَادَةَ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ أَنَسٍ، عَنْ أُمِّ سُلَيْمٍ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ خَادِمُكَ أَنَسٌ ادْعُ اللَّهَ لَهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اللَّهُمَّ أَكْثِرْ مَالَهُ وَوَلَدَهُ وَبَارِكْ لَهُ فِيمَا أَعْطَيْتَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard Qatadah narrating from Anas, from Umm Sulaym, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, your servant Anas, supplicate to Allah for him." So he said: "O Allah, increase his wealth and his children, and bless him in what You have given him."

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2480 b, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو دَاوُدَ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، سَمِعْتُ أَنَسًا، يَقُولُ قَالَتْ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ خَادِمُكَ أَنَسٌ ‏.‏ فَذَكَرَ نَحْوَهُ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: I heard Anas saying: Umm Sulaym said, "O Messenger of Allah, your servant Anas..." and he mentioned similarly.

reference: Sahih Muslim, hadith 2480 c, book 44, باب مِنْ فَضَائِلِ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رضى الله عنه ‏‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ، حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، سَمِعْتُ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ، يَقُولُ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ ‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Zayd: I heard Anas ibn Malik say the like of that.
